title: Test Harness
summary: Fast, offline Vitest unit tests across packages/, wired into npm test and npm run check so a failing test blocks a task, plus first tests on shared order transitions, JWT helpers and the internal token middleware.

acceptanceCriteria.text: npm test from the root runs every package's unit tests, prints per-file results and exits 0 when all pass.
A failing assertion makes npm test exit non-zero and name the failing file and test.
A failing assertion makes npm run check report FAIL and exit non-zero; restored, it passes.
A new src/**/*.test.ts in a package without tests runs with no config or package.json edit.
With Docker stopped and no network, all tests pass; no test opens a socket to a database, Kafka or model API.
The whole unit suite completes in 30 seconds or less on the dev machine.
Order transitions: all listed accepted, at least 3 unlisted (incl. from terminal) rejected, every status has an entry.
JWT: round trip verifies; expired, wrong-secret and modified tokens rejected; expiry uses controlled time.
Internal token middleware: right token passes, missing/wrong gets 401, /health open; unset token behaviour pinned.
Each AC-7..AC-9 test seen failing by briefly breaking the code; recorded in tasks.md.
npm run build succeeds and no test file ends up in any build output or Docker image.
testing-strategy.md, tech-stack.md, CLAUDE.md and README.md describe the real npm test.

openQuestions.text: Frontend in scope? Proposed: pure TS modules only, Node environment, no DOM tests.
First tests = order transitions, JWT, internal token middleware in shared? Proposed: yes.
Should npm test also run the spec dashboard tests? Proposed: no; npm run check runs both.
Coverage gate or report? Proposed: neither for now.
Is 30 s the right unit-suite budget? Proposed: yes.
